text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- The government plans to pass a law extending police powers before the summer. Justice Minister Nikolaus Michalek says the law should be limited to five years.
- The government will lose majority control of Austrian Airlines if it does not take part in a planned capital increase.
- Austria's economy is on the march again. Economic research institute WIFO is sticking to its forecast that the country's GDP will grow 2.2 percent in 1998.
- The Environment Ministry plans to sell loans worth 17.6 billion schillings from the water-supply fund.
- A draft savings bank law is ready, however it is not sure whether it will be assessed at all.
- Swiss cement maker Holderbank plans to become the number two in the market in eastern Austria.
- Lower Austria's Landesbank-Hypothekenbank is ready for cooperation with Oesterreichische Volksbanken AG after it has presented its results for 1996.
DIE PRESSE
- The number of early retirements is going down again as a result of the government's austerity measures. The average age of a male Austrian retiring has risen to 58 years.
- Austria's current account deficit has widened in the first four months of 1997 as the country's citizens spend too much money abroad.
- The Interior Ministry has reaffirmed that Austria is prepared for membership in the European Union's Schengen agreement.
- President Thomas Klestil said at a meeting of the Industrialist Association the country must stabilise its budget first in order to secure its importance as an industrial location.

- United Telekom Austria is not interested in bidding for the country's third mobile phone licence as it holds a stake in mobile phone company max.mobil. Meanwhile it is preparing the start of Austria's first private telephone network.
KURIER

- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary in the Finance Ministry, said he plans to continue the government's reforms of the public sector. At the same time civil servants in the Finance Ministry have postponed another demonstration.
- Banks demand builder Rober Rogner must retreat from all his current projects in order to secure his company's financial future.

- The government's holding and privatisation company OeIAG has doubled its profits to 1.7 billion schillings in 1996. Austria Tabak, Post & Telekom Austria and postal savings bank PSK are the next to be privatised.

- Economic research institute IHS head Bernhard Felderer says the government is on the right track to reform the public pension system. He says, the expansion of company pension schemes is "absolutely sensible".
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Tax evasion is expected to amount to 70 billion schillings this year. The Finance Ministry plans to introduce harder punishments to put an end to this.

- Austrian companies see good chances for investments in South Africa. Vienna's listed airport Flughafen Wien plans to participate in South African airports, while gamblers Novomatic and Casinos Austria hope to receive gambling licences there.
